I. Background and Introduction
On February 9, 1972, President Nixon issued Executive Order 11644 (37 F.R. 2877), noting a rapid increase in the use of off-road vehicles (ORVs) on public lands and recognizing that ORV use conflicts with resource conservation, environmental values, and other recreational uses of the public domain. The President called for a "unified Federal policy" towards ORV use on public land -- a policy that would regulate ORV use to protect resources, promote the safety of all users of public lands, and minimize the conflicts between users. Executive Order 11644 directs agency heads with jurisdiction over public lands to specify areas as open or closed to ORV use, and issue regulations prescribing operating conditions on open areas.
The Secretary of the Interior's memorandum of May 5, 1972, implements E.O. 11644. It directs Assistant Secretaries to review existing regulations governing ORV use on lands under their jurisdictions, to categorize all lands as either open or closed to ORV use, and to recommend for adoption regulations that will protect resources and minimize conflicts between ORVs and other uses of the public lands. The memorandum also requires appropriate Interior Bureaus to submit regulations and administrative guidelines that will implement the Executive Order on the lands which they administer.
